solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Journalist's robust idea abridged when broadcast

definitions.note: read as 'journalist is', the definition then links to the wordplay

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered about, so these letters are strewn into a new order
an abridged word is cut short, so the final letter of idea goes

explanation.surface: A reporter's strong concept, cut down for radio or television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abridged' cuts IDEA to IDE; ROBUST + IDE is rearranged ('when broadcast') into the newspaper job title.
explanation.definitionFit: A sub-editor is a newspaper staffer who corrects and trims copy, a kind of journalist.

clue.text: Mount a conference?

definitions.meaning: a mount is a mountain, whose top is the peak
a meeting of heads of government

explanation.definitionFit: The highest point of a mountain and a top-level meeting of leaders share this one word.

clue.text: Wild bear-cub beginning to eat food outdoors

indicators.note: wild suggests something unruly, so the letters of bear-cub run loose into a new order
the beginning of eat is its first letter

explanation.surface: A wild young bear starting to tuck into a picnic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges BEARCUB to BARBECU; 'beginning to' takes E from eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbecue is a meal grilled and eaten in the open air.

clue.text: Dock item

definitions.meaning: to dock an animal is to cut off its tail
a single point or particular in a list

explanation.definitionFit: A detail is a particular item; and to de-tail is to dock, a punning second sense.

clue.text: Worked on farm, drew about two pounds

indicators.note: about means around, so the drawn-game word goes round the pounds

parts.note: a team that drew a match tied it
L is the abbreviation for a pound (libra), so two of them make LL

explanation.surface: A farmhand worked the land and was paid a couple of pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Tilled land has been ploughed and prepared, farm work in the past tense.

clue.text: Retribution for pair is set in concrete

indicators.note: something set in concrete is embedded inside it, so these letters go into the other word

parts.note: concrete as an adjective means real, actual
taken as written

explanation.surface: Revenge for a couple's crime is fixed in stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprisal is an act of retaliation, retribution for a wrong.

clue.text: Means to make a bundle from crops

definitions.text: Means to make a bundle from crops

parts.words: Means to make a bundle from crops
parts.note: making a bundle suggests making a fortune, but it is the farm machine that bundles hay or straw

explanation.definitionFit: A baler is a machine that compresses harvested hay or straw into bales.

clue.text: Brendan's changed direction, but still in packaging

indicators.note: changed letters are altered in position, so the name and the compass point are mixed together

parts.note: the name Brendan, its 's read as 'has'
W for west, one of the compass directions

explanation.surface: Brendan has altered his course, though he is still wrapped up.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Brendan's reads as 'has'; 'changed' rearranges BRENDAN and W into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something still in its packaging is unused and new from the shop.

clue.text: Left hospital department with one-fifty pulse, dry

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
I is the Roman numeral for one
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A patient leaves the ward with a pulse of 150 and a dry mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Lentils are pulses, edible seeds sold dried.

clue.text: Watch salesman with consumer

parts.note: a rep is a travelling sales representative
an eater is one who consumes food

explanation.surface: A travelling salesman keeps an eye on a shopper.
explanation.definitionFit: A repeater is a pocket watch that chimes the time again when a button is pressed.

clue.text: Malcolm embracing woman who's being educated about marriage

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so the short name goes around the woman

parts.note: Mal is a short form of Malcolm
Rita is the heroine of Willy Russell's play and film Educating Rita

explanation.surface: Malcolm hugging a woman at college about their wedding plans.
explanation.walkthrough: Educating Rita is a British play and film about a hairdresser studying literature with the Open University.
explanation.definitionFit: Marital is the adjective for things relating to marriage.

clue.text: Could be gentler to spectacles when handled

indicators.note: could be says these letters might form something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A soft touch suits glasses when you hold them.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is witty: a lorgnette is a pair of glasses held up by a handle.
explanation.definitionFit: A lorgnette is a pair of glasses on a long handle, held to the eyes rather than worn.

clue.text: Delighted being second, then went in front

parts.note: a tick is a moment, a second in time
to have led is to have gone first

explanation.surface: A runner pleased at coming second, then taking the lead.
explanation.definitionFit: To be tickled is to be amused or pleased, a mild synonym for delighted.

clue.text: One tee shirt?

parts.note: a single is one of something
tee is the spelt-out name of the letter T

explanation.surface: A question about owning just one T-shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A singlet is a sleeveless vest, a shirt of sorts, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Won't wash, as bath without plug

definitions.meaning: an argument that won't wash is unconvincing
an unplugged bath lets everything drain away

explanation.definitionFit: An unconvincing argument is leaky; a plugless bath literally lets the contents drain.

clue.text: Desmond's flipping work! Habitual response is high-handed

parts.note: Des is a short form of Desmond

indicators.note: flipping something over turns it the other way, so the work word reads backwards

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
a tic is an involuntary habitual twitch

explanation.surface: Desmond swears at his job, a habitual outburst that comes across as overbearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a mild oath but turns OP into PO.
explanation.definitionFit: Despotic means tyrannical, behaving in a high-handed, autocratic way.

clue.text: Hazel's case has teachers appearing before she will

indicators.note: appearing before puts the teachers ahead of the next piece

parts.note: the NUT was the National Union of Teachers, a British teaching union
she'll is the contraction of she will

explanation.surface: Hazel's legal case involves teachers, then her own appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: Hazel looks like a woman's name but is the tree, whose nut has a hard case.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard outer covering of a hazelnut is its shell, the case around the kernel.

clue.text: Under pressure, has to collect artist with second edition

indicators.note: to collect is to gather in, so the artist is held inside

parts.note: taken as written
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A stressed editor must gather an artist for the reprint.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone harassed is stressed and pressured by repeated demands.

clue.text: Persistence of number taking a large town

parts.note: ten is a number
taken as written
a city is a large town

explanation.surface: The persistence of a figure taking over a big town.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenacity is dogged determination, refusing to let go, which is persistence.

clue.text: Lessen a Tory's hold on another politician

indicators.note: the words hold the answer, the 's reading as has: these words have it inside them

explanation.surface: Weaken a Conservative's grip over a rival lawmaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' points back to Tory; the answer runs across LESSEN A TORY.
explanation.definitionFit: A senator sits in a senate, a politician other than the Tory named.

clue.text: It has only one eye but that's not the point

definitions.text: It has only one eye but that's not the point

parts.words: It has only one eye but that's not the point
parts.note: a one-eyed creature is suggested, but the eye is a threading hole and the point is literally its sharp end

explanation.definitionFit: A sewing needle has a single eye for thread and a sharp point at the other end.

clue.text: Study group remains at loggerheads

indicators.note: parties at loggerheads are in conflict, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A study group is still quarrelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminar is a small class meeting to discuss a subject, a study group.

clue.text: 18 represented in pen by Latin American

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs
US means American

explanation.surface: A needle is drawn in ink by a Latin American.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 is the answer to 18 Down: the needle of a record player is this.
explanation.definitionFit: A stylus is the needle that tracks a record's groove on a turntable.

clue.text: Cat right on rodent's tail

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed after, at the tail

parts.note: a mouse is a rodent

explanation.surface: A cat is hard on the heels of a mouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A mouser is a cat kept or valued for catching mice.

clue.text: Park officer made a dash before German fellow left

indicators.note: before places the dash ahead of the next piece

parts.note: to run is to dash; ran is past tense

indicators.note: left as in departed, so the fellow goes from the word German

parts.note: taken as written
a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: A park keeper sprinted off before a German man departed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' removes MAN from GERMAN, leaving GER.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranger is a warden who patrols a national park.

clue.text: Too quick replacing the savoury — not acceptable

indicators.note: replacing means placing differently, so the remaining letters are put back in a new order
U means acceptable, upper-class usage, so it is dropped

explanation.surface: Swapping the savoury course was hasty and unacceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British label for upper-class, socially acceptable; 'not acceptable' drops it from THE SAVOURY, and 'replacing' rearranges THESAVORY.
explanation.definitionFit: Overhasty means rushing too much, acting too quickly.

clue.text: Heather's clothing remains striking

indicators.note: to clothe is to cover, so heather is wrapped around the remains

parts.note: ling is a name for heather
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: Heather's outfit of ashes is a striking look.
explanation.walkthrough: Heather looks like a woman's name but is the plant, also called ling.
explanation.definitionFit: Lashing means hitting or whipping, a striking action.

clue.text: Both sides needed to cover fish basket

indicators.note: both sides of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: A fish basket needs a lid on both sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needed to' is link; 'Both sides' of cover gives C and R, ahead of EEL. 'fish basket' looks like one phrase, but fish is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A creel is a wicker basket used by anglers to carry their catch.

clue.text: Ship stored rye at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A vessel's hold has rye stored in it on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: A destroyer is a fast warship.
